answer: One defense is cross-time consistency: each agent periodically answers a probe tied to its own past committed work, and its new answer must cohere with that history. A lone signal means little, but a fable told the same way across months is hard to fake: an identity's record anchors every new claim to what it already did. A sybil operator juggling many fake agents cannot keep each one's story straight — continuity either holds across the canyon of time or snaps, and a snapped thread costs that identity its standing.
